summary: Well‑executed, fully preregistered paired study that archived extensive artifacts and deterministically shows a ceiling outcome: every shared initial LLM candidate passed the deterministic validator (300/300), so the guarded single‑repair policy was never invoked and produced no measurable benefit. The experiment, analysis, and artifact publication appear internally consistent and reproducible from the supplied manifests and hashes. The manuscript correctly frames the ceiling result and lists limitations. However, the paper asserts a “multi‑vendor (Cisco IOS, JunOS, Arista)” manifest without an explicit, concise in‑manuscript summary (counts and representative vendor‑specific CLI evidence) that would allow readers to verify the multi‑vendor claim quickly without parsing the full task manifest. Minor clarification of the shared‑initial design consequences in one compact place of the main text would also improve clarity.
critical_issues: Manuscript asserts a multi‑vendor (Cisco IOS, JunOS, Arista) 300‑task manifest but does not present an explicit in‑paper vendor breakdown or short representative vendor‑specific examples; readers cannot quickly verify the multi‑vendor claim from the paper text alone (though the full task_manifest is archived). This is a required provenance/claim verification gap for a paper that markets itself as multi‑vendor.
required_revisions: Add a short, explicit in‑manuscript table or paragraph reporting vendor distribution (counts per vendor) and point to the canonical task_manifest path and SHA‑256 hash (execution/task_manifest.jsonl; SHA‑256 = 6d99060659a722e6a91dd2abd7baca45a2aefb41e124b049124d5ea2632cb4b3). Include 1–2 brief representative examples showing vendor‑specific CLI tokens or adapter annotations so the reader can verify vendor heterogeneity without unpacking the entire archive.

Add one concise clarifying sentence in Methods (or at the start of Results) that explicitly states the preregistered shared‑initial‑candidate design implies both arms used the identical initial generation per task, so the guarded arm can only change the outcome when that shared initial candidate fails validation (and note that this is why zero initial failures makes the guarded repair policy unexercised). Cite the paired_contingency_table.csv (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv; SHA‑256 = a39fd3386c945cae095f2f310ead1f21ac600f8b2492bcd49b664c8da5782aa0) in that sentence.
optional_revisions: Briefly summarize validator rule coverage (high‑level bullet list of rule families) and provide the validator artifact path and hash for rapid verification (execution/scoring/*.json already archived).

Add an explicit one‑paragraph recommendation in Limitations describing how an alternative design (independent initial draws per arm, larger repair budget, or harder/adversarial tasks) would change the estimand and interpretation, and point readers to the archived artifacts needed to reproduce such variants.
